evidence_layer: synthetic memory oracle: the original ARM bytes at 0xd21ec and 0x1f3f8c executed over staged .bss the GOT actually points at, with identical stubs on both arms; NOT device execution

covered: F1: self == *g_host and mode byte 0 -> global name table
F1: self != host -> local name table (hit, miss, -1)
F1: mode byte != 0 falls back to the local table (1 and 255)
F1: name pointer forwarded verbatim - non-empty, empty, NULL
F1: return value is the callee answer: slot 0 legal, -1 absent, INT_MIN untouched
F1: host pointer NULL + self NULL still takes the host branch
F2: id == -3 room chain - empty room, live head, destroyed, deactivated, both, all-dead, live head with a live next
F2: 0..99999 pass-through incl. both boundaries 0 and 99999
F2: id > 99999 hash - hit, neighbour bucket, chain end, walk-then-hit, NULL instance, destroyed, +0x69-only, INT_MAX
F2: bucket mask honoured (mask 3 vs 7) and 8 B bucket stride
F2: the failure byte 0x75505c is set on exactly one exit
F2: varid is dead - three cases with the same id and different varids produce identical records
not_covered: Code_Variable_Find_Slot_From_Local_Name semantics (stubbed): the CHashMap hash/compare and its -1 miss
Code_Variable_Find_Slot_From_Global_Name semantics (stubbed): the linear strcmp scan and "id = declaration order"
Object_Name semantics (stubbed), including its own "<undefined>" fallback at 0x330ac8
who writes 0x544be0 and 0x47f295 (no writer exists in .text)
not_applicable: F1 has no "lazy slot creation" arm: it is a dispatcher over two name tables and never touches the object's slot table.  The table==0 -> InternalGetYYVar path lives in Variable_GetValue_Direct and is covered by c/variable_direct/.
F2 does not consult g_ObjectHash at all; the only object-index consumer is Object_Name, which is stubbed.

g_run_room == NULL is undefined on the original bytes (0x1f4018 ldr r3,[r3] then 0x1f401c ldr r3,[r3,#0x80] would fault), so it is not a case: room_mode 0 stages a live CRoom with a NULL instance chain instead.

findings: F1 compares self against *one* global pointer and nothing else: no object field is read, so a pointer-equality test is the whole host test.  The fixture pins the degenerate case where the cell is NULL and self is NULL - it takes the host branch.
F1 forwards the name pointer with 0xd21fc mov r0,r1 and never inspects the string; empty and NULL names reach the callee unchanged.  Whether that is a hit or a miss is not this body's answer.
F2 never reads its second argument.  Three cases with id 100006 and varid 0 / 4242 / INT_MIN produce identical records.

F2 sets 0x75505c on exactly one of its five failure exits (0x1f407c, id == -3 with no live instance).  The other four leave it untouched - verified by reading the byte after every call, not by reading the card.
F2 is asymmetric on purpose: the id > 99999 hash path tests +0x68 only, so a deactivated instance (+0x69 != 0, +0x68 == 0) still yields its object name, while the room chain skips it.
card/byte agreement: both cards were re-checked against llvm-objdump instruction by instruction; see card_deltas.

card_deltas.claim: GOT 0x3edbbc -> .bss 0x544be0 (pointer, one extra ldr) and GOT 0x3edbc0 -> .bss 0x47f295 (byte, ldrb straight off the cell)
card_deltas.bytes: the image's GOT cells hold exactly 0x544be0 and 0x47f295, and 0xd21f4 is a third ldr while 0xd2210 is ldrb

card_deltas.claim: only self == *g_host AND mode == 0 uses the global table
card_deltas.bytes: 0xd2200 beq + 0xd2218 bne both fall back to 0xd2204; the global jump at 0xd221c is reachable only when both hold

card_deltas.claim: the second parameter (r1) is never read; 0x1f3fb8 overwrites it with the hash mask
card_deltas.bytes: no instruction in 0x1f3f8c..0x1f3fb4 names r1; 0x1f3fb8 is ldr r1, [r3, #0x4]

card_deltas.claim: six failure exits share one rodata string 0x3527e4, and only 0x1f407c sets 0x75505c
card_deltas.bytes: all six ldr/add pairs resolve to 0x3527e4, which holds exactly "<unknown_object>"; 0x1f407c is the only strb in the body

card_deltas.claim: the id > 99999 hash path checks +0x68 only, while the room chain checks +0x68 and +0x69
card_deltas.bytes: 0x1f3ff8 is the only ldrb on the hash path; 0x1f4038 and 0x1f4048 are the two on the room path

card_deltas.claim: node layout {next@+4, id@+8, inst@+0xc} and 8 B buckets

card_note: No card/byte delta.  Both cards' addresses, instruction counts, pool sizes, field offsets, GOT->.bss chains and return conventions match the pinned bytes; nothing had to be corrected on the byte side, and the cases here pin every one of those claims.
